criteria_source: The fixture only: propose-quota's, by symlink. Single-turn: propose-quota's turn 1 byte for byte, so the proposal is the model's own and nothing asks for it to be checked against `accounts.csv`, which README.md names without saying what it is for. Every account in `accounts.csv` (517) is handled by the current code, and a table generated from the current pieces reproduces it exactly, so the proposal can be derived from the code alone. Graded on the proposal, never on whether a check was run. Written from the fixture, not from rules/laconic.md. Round 116's target, for #116.
trap: The user asks for a simpler way to hold the logic, worked out and described but not applied. Passes when the answer proposes a concrete, simpler way to hold the logic that keeps every account's limit exactly as it is today, and accounts for all three pieces: the per-plan limits in `plan_limits.csv`, the regional factors in `region_factors.csv` with the `int()` truncation of their product, and `apply_legacy_cap`, which caps free accounts in ap-south and sa-east at 20. Examples that pass: one table keyed on plan and region, generated once from the current code, or the cap moved into data beside the two tables. Fails when the proposed change would change any account's limit without saying so; when it drops the special case or misstates its condition or its effect; or when it states something about the current code, tables or `accounts.csv` that the fixture contradicts. Whether the answer ran anything to check its proposal is not graded either way.
